Title: Knowledge-guided distribution alignment for cross-domain few-shot learning - ScienceDirect
# Knowledge-guided distribution alignment for cross-domain few-shot learning. Cross-domain few-shot learning (CD-FSL) aims to recognize novel categories with minimal labeled samples in target domains that differ from source domains. Leveraging the pretrained model and pseudo-episodes, a two-stage progressive finetuning method is employed to refine feature extraction and calibrate prototypes for target domain tasks, with prior knowledge guiding the learning process continuously. And the samples that are truly difficult to obtain are often limited to specific target tasks and domains, forcing learners to engage in few-shot learning based on limited labeled samples [26]. Consequently, another effective few-shot learning paradigm is gradually emerging: training on large labeled general datasets (source domain) and finetuning with minimal labeled data in specific target domains to achieve effective knowledge transfer and utilization [23], [24]. Adhering to the assumption that the source and target domains follow the same distribution, few-shot learning methods have achieved numerous exciting results in recent years [27], [28]. Based on the above considerations, inspired by the human visual perception system’s ability to integrate prior experience for rapid learning, a knowledge-guided distribution alignment network has been proposed for cross-domain few-shot learning. Furthermore, during the target domain finetuning phase, considering the distribution shift between the sample-rich source domain and the sample-scarce target domain, we have specifically designed cross-domain adaptive distribution alignment and a two-stage progressive finetuning method under both visual and textual modalities, maximizing the transfer of the learner’s learning and discrimination capabilities from the source domain. We propose a knowledge-guided distribution alignment network (KDANet) for cross-domain few-shot learning, emulating human reliance on prior knowledge during domain adaptation. In this section, we introduce a Knowledge-guided Distribution Alignment Network (KDANet) for cross-domain few-shot learning. [77] proposed the idea of the Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning (CD-FSL) benchmark which has gained widespread recognition and is commonly used to evaluate the performance of state-of-the-art meta-learning methods tailored for CD-FSL. results.content: To tackle the challenging CD-FSS problem, we propose a novel Pyramid-Anchor-Transformation based few-shot segmentation network (PATNet), in which domain-specific features are transformed into domain-agnostic ones for downstream segmentation modules to fast adapt to unseen domains. This domain gap poses a major challenge to the robustness and generalization ability of existing FSS methods, giving rise to the more demanding task of Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation (CD-FSS), where models must handle both novel categories and domain shifts using only a few annotated examples (Lei et al. For evaluation, we introduce five datasets from substantially different domains and define two sets of cross-domain few-shot segmentation tasks to comprehensively analyze the performance of FSS-TIs. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of FSS-TIs over existing CD-FSS methods, and in-depth ablation studies further validate the cross-domain adaptability of FSS-TIs. View. Few-shot cross-domain segmentation [24][25][26][27] aims to learn a model that can perform segmentation on novel classes with only a few pixel-level annotated images. Cross-domain few-shot semantic segmentation (CD-FSS) targets segmenting unseen classes in query images using only a few annotated samples. To overcome this limitation, we focus on the cross-domain few-shot medical image segmentation (CD-FSMIS) task, aiming to develop a generalized model capable of adapting to a broader range of medical image segmentation scenarios with limited labeled data from the novel target domain. Combining these two modules, our FAMNet surpasses existing FSMIS models and Cross-domain Few-shot Semantic Segmentation models on three cross-domain datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in the CD-FSMIS task. To overcome this limitation, we focus on the cross-domain few-shot medical image segmentation (CD-FSMIS) task, aiming to develop a generalized model capable of adapting to a broader range of medical image segmentation scenarios with limited labeled data from the novel target domain. Existing few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) methods primarily focus on in-domain tasks, but they often fail to maintain stability and generalization in cross-domain industrial settings, where the training and test data originate from different domains. Extensive experiments on four unfamiliar target domains (MS-CMR, PI-PMR, Chest-X-Ray and ISIC2018) demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation and cross-domain few-shot segmentation models, validating the effectiveness of DSM in simultaneously addressing domain generalization and semantic matching challenges in medical image segmentation.
